survey: A pair of orange flip-flops lying side by side on an unseen ground plane, seen from the front and above at about 45°. The toe end points toward the bottom-left and the heel toward the top-right. Both soles have the same orientation and foreshortening. Their thick side edges show along the lower-left, which matches a camera above and in front. Each yellow V-strap starts at a short vertical toe post near the front of the sole. Its two arms rise and run back to slots cut into the top surface on either side of the mid-sole. The slots are drawn as foreshortened openings that lie flat on the sole. Rows of small round bumps cover the forefoot. They shrink and squash into ellipses as the sole recedes, and they follow the sole's curved outline. Both sandals share one viewpoint, their long axes stay parallel, and their heels recede by the same amount.
